question.problem:
Consider the sequence starting from ${a}_{1}=2$ with the property $\frac{{a}_{n+1}}{{a}_{n}}=\frac{1}{5}$ for all $n\ge 1.$ Write the sum to infinity $S$ of the terms of this sequence using sigma notation in terms of index $n.$

$S={\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }${{field-1}}
question.worked_solution:
Notice that the sequence is a geometric sequence since the ratio of any two successive terms is constant.

The first term of the sequence is ${a}_{1}=2,$ and the common ratio is

$$
r=\frac{{a}_{n+1}}{{a}_{n}}=\frac{1}{5}.
$$

Therefore, the general term ${a}_{n}$ can be expressed as

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{n} & ={a}_{1}{(r)}^{n-1} \\  & =2{(\frac{1}{5})}^{n-1} \\  & =2{(\frac{1}{5})}^{-1}{(\frac{1}{5})}^{n} \\  & =10{(\frac{1}{5})}^{n}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the infinite geometric series  $S$  can be written in sigma notation as

$$
\begin{aligned}S={\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }{a}_{n} & ={\sum }_{n=1}^{\infty }10{(\frac{1}{5})}^{n}.\end{aligned}
$$
